# Dark mode is here

You asked for this more than for anything else. About 3,400 requests since we opened the feedback board in March, roughly four times the runner-up. As of version 2.4, Quill has a dark theme.

It took longer than it should have, and the reason is boring. Our editor stored note text as HTML with inline styles baked in from wherever you pasted them. Flip the background to near-black and half your older notes turned into gray-on-gray mush. So before we could ship a theme, we had to change how pasted content stores color: it now keeps a semantic role — body, quote, code — instead of a hex value, and the theme resolves that at render time. Old notes migrate the first time you open them.

Two things worth knowing.

The dark background is #16171A, not pure black. Pure black under white text produces halation, that smeary glow around the letterforms, and it's worse if you have astigmatism. A slightly lifted gray fixes it without looking washed out.

Second, it follows your system setting by default. If you'd rather pin it, Settings > Appearance has Light, Dark, and System, plus a schedule if you want the switch to happen at sunset.

Code blocks got their own pass. The old syntax colors were tuned for a white page and looked radioactive on a dark one, so we dropped the saturation and re-checked every pair for contrast.

Update from the App Store, or wait a day and it'll land on its own.

# Dark mode has landed

No other request came close. Since the feedback board opened in March we've logged about 3,400 asks for it, roughly four times whatever sat in second place. Version 2.4 gives Quill a dark theme.

The delay has a dull explanation. Our editor kept note text as HTML, inline styles and all, carried over from wherever you copied it. Drop the background to near-black and half your archive turned into gray smeared on gray. So the theme had to wait on a change to how pasted content records color: it now stores a semantic role — body, quote, code — rather than a hex value, and the theme resolves that role when it draws. Older notes convert the first time you open them.

Two details worth knowing.

The background is #16171A rather than pure black. White text on true black causes halation, the smeary glow that creeps out from the letters, and astigmatism makes it worse. Lifting the gray a notch clears it up and still doesn't look faded.

Second, it tracks your system setting unless you say otherwise. Settings > Appearance holds Light, Dark, and System, along with a schedule if you'd like it to flip at sunset.

Code blocks needed separate attention. The old syntax palette was picked for a white page and glowed on a dark one, so we pulled the saturation down and rechecked every pair for contrast.

Grab it from the App Store today, or leave it a day and the update will arrive on its own.
